title: IRWD Q3 Earnings Beat, Revenues Miss, 2026 View Raised, Stock Up
author: Na
description: Ironwood Pharmaceuticals reported Q3 adjusted EPS of 36 cents, beating consensus estimates of 30 cents, though revenues missed expectations at $133 million. The company raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $485-$510 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance to over $350 million, driven by strong Linzess prescription demand growth of 4.9% year-over-year. The stock rose 6.9% following the announcement.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company beat EPS estimates (36 cents vs. 30 cents consensus), raised full-year 2026 revenue and EBITDA guidance, demonstrated strong Linzess prescription demand growth of 4.9% YoY, and increased U.S. collaboration profit by 8.6%. Stock price rose 6.9% post-announcement.

AbbVie is mentioned as Ironwood's partner in the Linzess collaboration, sharing profits equally. The positive Linzess sales performance benefits both companies, but AbbVie is not the primary focus of the article.
Mentioned as a comparison stock with a higher Zacks Rank #1 rating, but no specific news or performance data is provided about the company itself. Stock has declined 45.7% year-to-date.

title: Will Linzess Continue to Aid Ironwood's Top-Line Growth in Q3?
author: Na
description: Ironwood Pharmaceuticals (IRWD) is experiencing strong prescription demand for its primary product Linzess, with U.S. net profit share surging 72.6% year-over-year in the first half of 2026. The company raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $460-$485 million, citing continued momentum from Linzess sales, recent FDA label expansion for pediatric patients, and favorable pricing dynamics. IRWD stock is trading at a valuation discount to the industry and carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong 72.6% year-over-year profit growth from Linzess sales, raised 2026 revenue guidance, recent FDA pediatric label expansion creating new market opportunities, favorable pricing dynamics, and trading at a valuation discount to industry peers support positive outlook.

AbbVie is a partner in Linzess commercialization with equal profit/loss sharing, benefiting from strong Linzess demand, but the article focuses primarily on Ironwood's performance rather than AbbVie's specific impact.
Astellas has a regional partnership for Linzess commercialization in Japan with royalty arrangements, but limited information provided about performance or impact.
AstraZeneca holds commercialization rights for Linzess in China with royalty payments to Ironwood, but minimal detail provided regarding regional performance or contribution.

title: PGEN vs. IRWD: Which Biotech Stock Offers Better Growth Potential?
author: Na
description: Precigen (PGEN) and Ironwood Pharmaceuticals (IRWD) are biotech companies heavily dependent on single marketed drugs. Precigen's Papzimeos generated $74.6 million in revenues in H1 2026 with strong growth momentum and market exclusivity until 2032, while Ironwood's Linzess saw a 72.6% year-over-year profit surge. Precigen is rated as the better investment pick with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) versus Ironwood's Rank #2 (Buy), offering clearer long-term growth prospects despite higher valuation multiples.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong early commercial momentum with Papzimeos generating $74.6M in H1 2026 revenues and doubling sequentially in Q2. Product has FDA market exclusivity until 2032, first-in-class position, and pipeline potential through AdenoVerse platform. Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) with rising earnings estimates and 92.6% year-to-date stock performance.

Linzess demonstrated healthy demand with 72.6% year-over-year profit surge in H1 2026, leading to raised full-year revenue guidance. Patent protection until March 2029 and label expansion opportunities support continued growth. However, heavy reliance on single product and pipeline uncertainty limit upside compared to Precigen. Zacks Rank #2 (Buy).

Developing INO-3107 as a competing therapy for RRP with FDA decision expected October 30, 2026. Represents potential future competitive threat to Precigen's Papzimeos market position but remains in development stage with uncertain approval outcome.

title: 3 Stocks Trading Near $5 With Massive Earnings Upside
author: Chris Markoch
description: The article identifies three penny stocks trading near $5 with significant earnings growth potential in 2026. Transocean Ltd. (RIG) is expected to grow earnings by 100% driven by favorable oil market conditions. B2Gold Corp. (BTG), a junior miner, is forecast to grow earnings by 74% as mining stocks catch up with gold prices. Ironwood Pharmaceuticals Inc. (IRWD) is projected to achieve 150% earnings growth following a 40% increase in revenue guidance, though it trades above consensus price targets.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Expected 100% earnings growth, first profitable quarter in five quarters, recent analyst price target increase from $5 to $6, and favorable oil market conditions in 2026 support strong upside potential.
Forecast 74% earnings growth with expected catch-up trade as mining stocks lag gold prices. Up 86% in 12 months and positioned to benefit from precious metals catalysts in 2026.

Projected 150% earnings growth following 40% revenue guidance increase in January. Despite trading 20% above consensus target, analyst price targets have increased significantly and key Phase 3 trial expected in 2026.

title: Stock Market Today: S&P 500, Nasdaq, WTI Crude Futures Advance After US Strike On Venezuela— GH Research, Vertiv Holdings, Nukkleus In Focus (UPDATED)
author: Rishabh Mishra
description: U.S. stock futures rose on Monday as major indices opened the first full trading week of 2026 higher. Following the U.S. strike on Venezuela and removal of President Maduro, crude oil prices fluctuated around $57.29 per barrel. Several stocks gained attention: Vertiv Holdings jumped on an upgrade, GH Research soared on FDA update news, Nukkleus rose after acquiring Israeli defense software, Ironwood advanced on positive FY26 guidance, and Brand Engagement Network climbed on a new vendor agreement. JPMorgan's outlook suggests continued but challenged strength in U.S. equities, with potential 10-15% corrections offset by year-end gains driven by AI-related spending.
